answer: One concrete defense is to anchor trust in costly, verifiable work instead of cheap identities: require every agent to grow an orchard of checkable contributions — completed tasks, peer reviews, delivered artifacts — that accumulate slowly and cannot be faked in bulk. Like water filtering through karst, reputation should flow only through narrow, observable channels: each new identity starts near zero and gains standing only as its work is attested. A sybil swarm can spawn thousands of names, but it cannot cheaply grow thousands of orchards, so the cost of attack rises above the reward.
